subject: Recap: ApexCare executive briefing — outcomes, risks & procurement path
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Susan Park <susan.park@apexcare.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@apexcare.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: ApexCare executive briefing — outcomes, risks & procurement path

Hi Susan / Tom —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Below is a concise recap from our exec briefing and the recommended path forward so we have alignment across legal/procurement and the engineering review next week. Please reply with any corrections, or confirm and we’ll lock next dates.

Key business outcomes discussed
- Improve patient intake NLP accuracy from ~72% to >90% on triage intents (primary KPI).
- Reduce average inference latency for real-time triage assistant to <250ms p99.
- Decrease inference cost per 1k clinical messages by ~40% through batching and quantization options.

Primary pain points you highlighted
- Current vendor has inconsistent latency spikes during peak hours, causing timeouts in the mobile triage flow.
- Data residency & auditability required for specific payer-linked datasets.
- Procurement needs clarity on SLAs, indemnity, and SOC2 artifacts before legal signs off.

Risks & mitigations we proposed
- Risk: Latency spikes at scale → Mitigation: Dedicated GPU lane for production + smart routing fallback to a slightly lower-cost variant to preserve availability.
- Risk: Sensitive payer data → Mitigation: Private deployment option (VPC) + KMS integration and per-customer audit logs; we’ll include evidence artifacts you asked for.
- Risk: Procurement timeline slipping → Mitigation: Standard mutual action plan (MAP) with checkpoints; I’ve attached the initial MAP (v1) and the SOC2 evidence request you asked for.

Procurement path & timeline (recommended)
1) This week — Technical deep-dive with ApexCare infra & security (90m) — proposed dates: Tue/Wed next week.
2) Week after — Proof-of-concept (4-week pilot) scoped to triage intent set; dedicated capacity + telemetry.
3) Contracting — Use MAP to align milestones; target PO within 6 weeks of pilot start pending legal sign-off.

Open asks (action owners)
- ApexCare: Confirm 2x preferred slots for technical review and internal procurement lead (Tom / procurement@apexcare.com). (ApexCare)
- Redwood: Share SOC2 artifact + sample MSA redline template; provide pilot SOW draft. (Mateo / Priyom)
- Redwood: Assign engineering lead for the technical call — looping in Lauren for deployment/runbook questions. (Lauren)

Next steps (immediate)
- I’ll schedule the technical deep-dive for Tuesday 11/31 (alternate Wed 12/1) pending your confirmation.
- Priyom will attach the pilot SOW and a preliminary pricing appendix after this thread.

Attachments: ApexCare_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx; SOC2-evidence-request.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Dr. Susan Park <susan.park@apexcare.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@apexcare.com>, procurement@apexcare.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: ApexCare executive briefing — outcomes, risks & procurement path

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the tidy recap — this captures the discussion well. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Procurement timeline: We’re targeting end-of-quarter PO issuance (EoQ) but that requires receiving SOC2 artifacts and an MSA redline by next Thursday.
- Security: Our cloud compliance team will need to validate KMS/HSM details and any data masking approaches for payer PHI before pilot provisioning.
- Cost: The 40% reduction sounds reasonable as a target; can we get a mid-pilot checkpoint for cost/latency tradeoffs?

Action items from ApexCare
- I’ll confirm the security stove-pipe owner for the technical call (expecting to be Nora Lee from Compliance).
- Tom (cc’d) — can procurement confirm the PO window and whether we can do a short pre-PO agreement (NDA + commercial terms) to unblock the pilot?

Tom — loop in procurement@apexcare.com if you want to propose exact contract leads.

Susan
Dr. Susan Park
Chief Innovation Officer, ApexCare
susan.park@apexcare.com | +1 (202) 555-0123

Susan / Tom —

Appreciate the quick reply and the helpful clarity on timelines. A few updates from our side and confirmations for the technical deep-dive: 

1) Technical deep-dive scheduling- Proposed slots (PST): Tue 12/1 09:00–10:30 or Wed 12/2 13:00–14:30. Agenda will cover: workload profile, telemetry needs, SSO/KMS mapping, and pilot success criteria. Lauren will lead the deployment/runbook section.

2) SOC2 / artifacts- Attached is the SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (list of items we will provide) and a pointer to our SOC2 summary. Priyom will share the MSA redline and pilot SOW by EOD Monday to give your legal and procurement team time to review.

3) MAP & pilot SOW- Attached: ApexCare_MutualActionPlan_v1.xlsx — high-level milestones and decision gates. We anticipate the pilot to include: 1x dedicated GPU pool, telemetry dashboard, and a 4-week evaluation window scoped to triage intents.

4) Risk clarifications- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS in our Private deployment and can provide HSM-backed key options; we’ll document key rotation and access logs for auditing.
- Latency: For pilot, we’ll allocate a reserved lane to reduce variance and run a short burst test to validate p99.

5) Commercials & contracting- Priyom (cc’d) — I’ve looped you in for the MSA and SOW redlines. Priyom, can you include an initial pilot price appendix with a clear conversion path to reserved monthly billing?

Immediate asks- ApexCare: Confirm which of the two proposed slots works and who from security will join.
- Redwood: Priyom to send MSA redline + pilot SOW by EOD Monday (11/30).

We’ll hold off on final vendor configuration until we get confirmation on the technical call attendees — thanks.

Best,
Mateo
